implementationPlan.description: 1. Add named worktree readiness probes and tests first (DoD1–2 plus latest gate requirement). Extend ProbeResult with info and emit [INFO]; existing pass/warn/fail meanings stay unchanged. Read .moe/project.json once without starting StateManager; absent file/settings uses WT01 resolver default; malformed JSON, unreadable file or invalid mode gets a named settings failure, never silently enables/off-defaults. Resolve target via landed WT01 resolveWorktreeTarget (literal trimmed consolidationBranch else main), do not duplicate its policy. Reuse runGit with argv, canonical cwd, timeout <=2s/call and <=128KiB output; For error handling, report bounded single-line error categories without dumping config/stdout. New labels: worktree git version, project root, control branch, target, quality gate. Check parsed git --version >=2.38 (Windows/Apple suffix allowed; malformed unknown fails), realpath project == rev-parse --show-toplevel, symbolic-ref -q HEAD exactly refs/heads/moe/control, and target is a valid fully-qualified local branch ref resolving to a commit. Require nonblank settings.qualityGate when on; do not execute it. Run worktree list --porcelain -z once, parse NUL fields/blank-record delimiters (never split a filename on whitespace/newlines), and fail target probe if any branch field equals refs/heads/<target>, including current checkout; detached roots are not target checkouts. Missing ref, timeout/truncated/malformed listing and spawn errors are named failures on, information off. All new worktree probe results are [INFO] with observed condition when mode off; they never change old probe severity/exit logic. Tests through runDoctor with stubbed read-only runner cover each failure individually on/off, all passing on exits0, absent settings preserves current health fixtures, absent/blank gate fails on, invalid mode/config not silently defaulted, version boundaries/suffixes, custom/glob/default target, and no shell/network/mutating command invocation.

implementationPlan.description: 2. Add conservative stale terminal-worktree warning (DoD3). Reuse the successful listing from step1; inspect only registered immediate canonical .worktrees/<full task-id> paths within this project, not arbitrary human names, outside roots, symlink escapes, prefix lookalikes or unregistered directories. Read corresponding regular .moe/tasks/<id>.json without writes; match record id, terminal status DONE/ARCHIVED and finite updatedAt older than strictly 24h. Using updatedAt is a conservative age bound because no archivedAt exists; document that fact in the probe message/comment. Count/name stale entries with [WARN] when on and [INFO] when off; exactly24h, future time, recent terminal, live tasks are not stale. Unreadable/invalid/missing task data or missing timestamp gives bounded 'age unknown' informational/soft warning, never a hard failure or deletion permission. Table-driven tests cover DONE and ARCHIVED, old-but-live, boundary times, missing/malformed JSON/id mismatch, nested/foreign paths and UNC/drive normalization. Add one real throwaway Git fixture for listing/target detection (path with spaces, task worktree and separate target checkout), preserving existing HTTP/socket cleanup. Snapshot source JSON bytes/mtimes, refs and index before/after doctor to prove read-only; clean only owned fixture after all processes exit.
implementationPlan.note:
Step 2 done (the governor's 06:10Z ruling: steps 1-2 only, then BLOCKED on WT-10M).
- New probe 'worktree stale task worktrees' reuses step 1's listing.
- It considers only registered worktrees whose realpath'd dirname equals <root>/.worktrees (isSameProjectPath, so D:/ vs /mnt/d and //wsl$ shares match) and whose basename is task-*.
- It reads .moe/tasks/<id>.json (regular file, id match). A task counts as stale when it is DONE or ARCHIVED and updatedAt is strictly more than 24h old. updatedAt is a conservative bound because tasks have no archivedAt; a code comment says so.
- Severity: [WARN] when on, [INFO] when off. Unknown age (missing or malformed record, id mismatch, bad timestamp) is [INFO]. It never fails and never deletes.
- I compacted the step 1 code at the same time. Both functions are realpathSync.native now, so Windows 8.3 TEMP paths match git's toplevel.
Tests:
- 12-row age table: DONE/ARCHIVED 25h, 24h+1ms, exactly 24h, 1h, future, WORKING 72h, plus the unknown cases.
- Ignore table: nested, foreign, lookalike, human name, control root. A symlink escape row (skipped on win32). A cross-spelling row. The off-mode stale row is folded into the off table.
- Real Git fixture, under a path with spaces: a task worktree plus a separate target checkout. It gives a target FAIL and a stale WARN with exit 1. The snapshot of project.json/task bytes+mtimes, .git/index, HEAD, refs and the worktree list is unchanged after doctor. After the worktree is removed, the target is OK and the exit code is 0.
Evidence, from snapshot /tmp/wt16.fqfUXx (HEAD archive, native npm ci, env -i, node 24.21.0):

implementationPlan.description: 3. Write the operator runbook (DoD4, corrected by latest comments). Add TOC entry and `Worktree mode: flip on / roll back` section to TROUBLESHOOTING.md from FINAL landed WT-S §7.3/7.4 and actual WT10M CLI. Explain info/off vs hard/on probes, required fast-per-landing qualityGate, git>=2.38/root/moe/control/free target, and soft stale warning (no automatic doctor cleanup). Flip: stop/drain all seats/open attempts and let REVIEW land/finalize; inspect git for-each-ref refs/moe/rescue and recover/archive live tasks first; through supported operator settings declare resources.git-land-main {capacity:1,maxLeaseMs:7200000,releaseOnDeregister:true} and configure gate; human runs Bash `scripts/moe-agent.sh --land-branch moe/work-2026-10-24` or PS `scripts/moe-agent.ps1 -LandBranch moe/work-2026-10-24`. Explain target must be ancestor of branch before flip so switch preserves dirty daemon files; conflict recovery merges main INTO the shared branch, never directly into main. Migration always gates in .moe-free candidate workspace, no task lease (drain), two-parent C, CAS/nonforced publish, no task ledger; on any failure/unknown stop flip, unknown settled by rerun, no force/manual push/reset. After confirmed branch inclusion use exact `git switch -c moe/control main`, set worktreeMode on and consolidationBranch main, run `node packages/moe-daemon/dist/index.js doctor`, restart only after pass. Rollback: drain, land remaining task branches or human preserve/merge them into non-main shared branch; set mode off, UNSET consolidationBranch (main is shared-mode opt-in), switch explicitly `git switch -c moe/work-<date> main` using fresh branch name; preserve worktrees/rescue refs until recovery, normal sweep handles terminal tasks. Pinned mismatch blocks for human. Rollback never moves main. No generic 'let peel run' alternative, no manual merge/push to main, no setting-default flip or wrappers edited by this task.

4. Single verification gate (DoD5 and epic rail2). From repo root run exactly `(cd packages/moe-daemon && npm run build && npx vitest run src/commands/doctor.test.ts) && (S=$(mktemp -d) && trap 'rm -rf "$S"' EXIT && git archive HEAD scripts | tar -x -C "$S" && (cd "$S" && bash scripts/tests/parity-check.sh))`. Require exit0, doctor tests actually executed, parity PASS; archive uses committed wrapper bytes because this slice changes none. Run the same doctor test on native Windows if the development gate was POSIX, pinning path/listing behavior; no WSL result mislabeled Windows. Load regression-check/verification-before-completion, retain fresh exact command/exitCode/outputTail. Check runbook commands/settings/ordering against the landed producer contracts without executing migration/rollback on this project. No full unrelated IDE/wrapper postflight gate; WT19 owns whole-epic integration.

5. Final adversarial self-review once. Load adversarial-self-review; attack unreadable/malformed project/task JSON, invalid gate/mode, fake Git version, detached HEAD, invalid/injection-like branch names, unrelated GIT_* environment, NUL parsing, output/time bounds, Windows case vs POSIX identity and terminal timestamp boundaries. Confirm new off-mode failures do not suppress existing health errors; on-mode unknown is never ready; doctor never writes .moe/Git or starts daemon. Audit runbook rollback's unset+switch order and migration's no-lease exception versus normal landing lease, no main bypass, no destructive recovery suggestions. Keep <=400 net LOC/three files. If fixes arise rerun same gate; complete via Moe with actual paths/fresh evidence, wrapper owns Git writes. WT17/18 keep other docs.

comments.content:
For WT-16's runbook, from WT-10M's planner (architect-6fc3dd5c). The migration CLI takes the land lease after all; see the contract comment on task-25388400. This replaces WT-S §7.3's "It takes no lease" for runbook step 4, because WT-10M's DoD 3 is human-owned. Runbook step 4 must: (a) Create a dedicated board row for the migration, e.g. "[migration] land moe/work-2026-10-24 on main". Move it to PLANNING and leave it unassigned. The fleet is already drained by step 1, so no seat claims it. (b) Run `scripts/moe-agent.sh --project

--land-branch moe/work-2026-10-24 --lease-task `, adding `--worker-id ` if wanted. The ps1 form is `-LandBranch … -LeaseTask …`. - Exit 0 with MOE_MIGRATION_LANDED or MOE_COMMIT_NOTHING_TO_COMMIT means main contains the branch. - Anything else stops the runbook before the flip. (c) Archive the row afterwards. Archiving also makes the daemon's reaper drop a lease that a killed run left behind. Codes to document: - MOE_MIGRATION_BAD_ARGS (exit 2). - MOE_MIGRATION_NO_GATE: no qualityGate, or MOE_DISABLE_QUALITY_GATE=1. - MOE_COMMIT_FAILED_LAND_LEASE. - MOE_LAND_FETCH_FAILED and MOE_LAND_TARGET_DIVERGED. - MOE_COMMIT_FAILED_CONFLICT: merge main into the branch, then re-run. - MOE_COMMIT_FAILED_GATE. - MOE_PUSH_FAILED. - MOE_PUSH_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN: re-run to settle it. - MOE_COMMIT_FAILED_REF_CONTENTION. - MOE_MIGRATION_LANDED. The resource declaration `git-land-main` in step 3 stays as written.

comments.author: architect-899a90d6
comments.content:
Planner note from architect-899a90d6, WT-19's rev-2 planner. It adds no scope and changes no files or DoD.

Step 1 reads the worktree mode through the WT-01 resolver. Pass it the whole parsed settings object, `resolveWorktreeMode(settings)`, never a reduced `{ worktreeMode }`.

Why: WT-19 rev 2 proposes a gate-aware default, pending the human's go: an unset worktreeMode resolves to 'on' only when settings.qualityGate is non-blank. A reduced object would hide the gate from the resolver, so doctor would judge that project as 'off' and skip the hard worktree probes. claimNextTask.ts:156 already passes state.project?.settings. WT-19's adversarial pass greps every caller for this.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: Extend the existing offline runDoctor with bounded read-only Git probes; no new command/service/schema/default change. Three files, <=60min and <=400 net LOC with table-driven tests. Pair diagnostics with precise operator flip/rollback steps. Latest WT-S comment-5957b3a6 overrides earlier text: gate required when on, migration has NO task lease, rollback must unset consolidationBranch and leave moe/control.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: doctor.ts currently has pass/warn/fail, runDoctor collects probes and fails only on fail; existing health tests have no project.json or Git repo, so absent settings must retain shared-mode success until WT19 default flips. Reuse util/cachedPlanPaths.ts runGit(args,cwd,timeout,maxBuffer), already masks GIT_* and global config, disables optional locks/network, uses pinned gitExecutable(). Do not use openProjectGit because it combines toplevel with trust checks and would hide separate named diagnostics. WT01 supplies resolveWorktreeMode and resolveWorktreeTarget; read their landed exports first. Task has updatedAt/completedAt/reviewCompletedAt but no archivedAt: stale terminal-age warning uses conservative updatedAt (state last changed) for both DONE/ARCHIVED; no false claim to know historic transition time. Git worktree porcelain -z documented at https://git-scm.com/docs/git-worktree .
planningNotes.risks: Read-only must be literal: no fetch, config write, cleanup, prune or fixes. Missing Git/config/malformed output must not look ready; worktree failures info only when mode is explicitly/default off, malformed mode is not silently off. Unknown stale-task data only warns. Cross-platform path comparisons use native normalized/real paths (case-insensitive Windows only), never POSIX blanket lowercase or translating WSL paths. Existing WT10M dependency now owns CLI; direct WT10 edge added per comment. WT-S/01/M unlanded contracts must be reread before implementation.
